name: Aeneas
overview: Aeneas is a male figure noted in the New Testament for being bedridden and paralyzed for eight years before receiving healing through the apostle Peter. Scripture highlights his physical condition and miraculous restoration, emphasizing God's power to heal. No additional tribal or familial details are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Aeneas' appears as a proper name in Acts 9:33 without an associated meaning provided in the biblical text or the given facts. Therefore, it is presented simply as his personal name without further etymological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Aeneas beyond what is mentioned in his unique attribute of being healed by Peter. No additional relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Aeneas's significance lies in his healing by Peter, which serves as a testament to the apostolic authority and the power of Christ working through His servants. His restoration from paralysis after eight years demonstrates God's mercy and the transformative impact of faith. This event contributes to the early church's witness of divine healing and the spread of the gospel.
